documentation.title: Documentation and Provenance
introParagraphs: A grading report describes the diamond’s identification and quality characteristics. It does not automatically establish ownership, purchase value, chain of custody or mining country.
When provenance or compliance documentation is important, specify this in the sourcing brief before receiving options.
The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme regulates international trade in rough diamonds. It should not be presented as automatic country-of-origin proof for every polished diamond.

items.question: Does Dalila Diamonds sell natural or laboratory-grown diamonds?
items.answer: Dalila Diamonds’ core wholesale offering is natural diamonds. The report description should always be checked to confirm that each selected stone is identified as natural.

items.question: Who can request wholesale loose diamonds?
items.answer: The service is intended for professional buyers such as jewellers, manufacturers, retailers, wholesalers, dealers and jewellery designers. Buyer eligibility is confirmed during the enquiry process.

items.question: Is there a minimum wholesale order?
items.answer: Minimum order requirements may depend on the diamond, quantity, sourcing route and destination. The applicable minimum should be confirmed in the written quotation rather than assumed.

items.question: Which grading reports are available?
items.answer: Available diamonds may carry reports from laboratories such as GIA, IGI or HRD Antwerp. Laboratory availability depends on the selected stone and sourcing request.

items.question: Can I verify the diamond report before purchasing?
items.answer: Yes. Buyers should verify the report number through the issuing laboratory’s official database and compare the retrieved information with the diamond offered.

items.question: Can Dalila source matched diamond pairs?
items.answer: Matched pairs and layouts can be requested. Provide acceptable tolerances for carat weight, measurements, colour, clarity, fluorescence, shape and overall appearance.

items.question: Why are wholesale diamond prices not displayed as one price per carat?
items.answer: Diamond pricing depends on more than carat weight. Shape, colour, clarity, cut, measurements, report, appearance, availability, quantity and logistics can all affect the quotation.

items.question: Can I request a diamond that is not in the live inventory?
items.answer: Yes. Submit the complete specifications through Dalila’s customised sourcing service when a suitable diamond is not available in the current inventory.

items.question: Does a grading report prove where a natural diamond was mined?
items.answer: Not usually. A standard grading report identifies and grades the stone but does not automatically confirm its mining country. Geographic-origin or provenance claims require separate supporting documentation.

items.question: How long does wholesale diamond delivery take?
items.answer: Timing depends on availability, inspection, payment, destination, carrier and customs processing. The expected dispatch and delivery window should be confirmed in the quotation before purchase.
